term: commission: reported commission versus Jesus' commissioning
resolution: The five report statements (STMT-REPORTED-MATT-16-CHURCH-ON-ROCK-KEYS-BINDING, STMT-REPORTED-MATT-18-CHURCH-JUDGES-DISCIPLES-BIND, STMT-REPORTED-MATT-COMMISSION-GROUNDED-IN-GIVEN-AUTHORITY, STMT-REPORTED-JOHN-20-SENDING-FORGIVE-RETAIN, STMT-REPORTED-JOHN-21-PETER-SHEPHERD) use the textual sense: what a Gospel says Jesus gave (DEF-COMMISSION-REPORT-POWERS). Two premises use both senses and bridge them. STMT-COMMISSION-REPORTS-GO-BACK-TO-JESUS asserts that the event (Commissioning.Gave, DEF-COMMISSION-EVENT-AND-GOVERNING-POWER) happened for the powers the reports name. STMT-HEAVEN-RATIFIED-ATTESTATION-CRITERION is weaker and asserts less: from independent reports that each name a heaven-ratified power, it gives the event for some such power, without saying which, to whom, or that any whole report goes back to Jesus, and the criterion can hold while the first premise fails (attestation_not_reports). STMT-CHURCH-FOUNDED-IN-COMMISSIONED-APOSTLES uses only the event sense. No step passes from a report to an event except through one of these two premises, and the substance of a commission (its powers) is meant, not its wording. A critical dating of a saying to 'a later period' (STMT-MATT-16-18-18-17-SAYINGS-LATER) is a statement about the saying, in neither of these senses of a power; the event-level STMT-JUDGING-POWER-NOT-GIVEN-BY-JESUS is a separate, unattributed proposition, and no record passes from the dating to it. It is not the report's own post-resurrection setting: a power the risen Jesus gave (John 20.21-23, Matthew 28.18-20) counts as Jesus' giving in Commissioning.Gave.
